AI agents are no longer just writing code—they are now designing 7 nm CPUs and executing live e-commerce checkouts.

Here are the key engineering and architecture updates in AI today:

🤖 Architect Labs unveiled Frostbite, an interaction net CPU designed entirely by AI. Agents handled the development pipeline from theoretical concepts to a 7 nm GDS file, achieving 4.59x performance per watt over an in-order core in pre-silicon testing.

🛍️ Meta's Muse agent can now shop on Walmart's website to find and purchase Black Friday deals on your behalf. Walmart is using its live Agent Gateway implementation to let the AI discover products without sharing your purchase history.

⚙️ Google AI launched a preview of Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API. Designed for large tool libraries, it allows agents to keep toolkits on standby and dynamically load parameter schemas on demand inside a single Interactions API request.

🧮 Claude successfully solved a 167-year-old math mystery, expanding the footprint of AI models into complex theoretical mathematics.

🔮 OpenAI's Chief Scientist issued a new prediction forecasting a massive AI avalanche arriving by 2027.

As developers, seeing agent capabilities shift from standard function calling toward dynamic schema retrieval and autonomous hardware layouts shows how fast modern AI infrastructure is maturing.

Which of these developments do you see having the biggest impact on your own workflow?
